items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like `reconcileQueryState` and `persisterRestoreMarker` are clear. But `isPersisterRestoreResult` is full of `(value as any)` casts and returns `PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>`. The reconcile logic, which compares data and error timestamps separately, has few comments explaining the rules.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Core lives in a separate `persisterRestore.ts`, but `reconcileQueryState(liveState: QueryState, persistedState: QueryState)` drops the TData/TError generics. `queryObserver.ts` and `types.ts` were changed too. Bulk restore in `createPersister` builds state inline via `queryCache.build(..., restoredState)` instead of sharing one helper with per-query restore.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No validation or normalisation of persisted state (counts, timestamps, fetchStatus); a malformed snapshot goes straight in. The `any` casts are on a public guard. The hidden test failed on the bulk merge case 'merged live data with newer persisted error metadata', so the reconcile edge cases are not handled correctly.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: `createPersisterRestoreResult` is exported and uses a Symbol marker, but also sets a forgeable `__persisterRestore: true` that the guard accepts. `data` and `state` are both optional. Bulk restore doesn't share one apply path, and the bulk-merge hidden test fails.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: New exports are additive (`createPersisterRestoreResult`, `isPersisterRestoreResult`, `reconcileQueryState`), and the existing persister tests pass (P2P 42/42). But `types.ts` and `createPersister.ts` changed, so the persister return type and the shape returned by persisterFn shifted internally.
